p.src: The story tells how Song Jiang, unwilling to betray Chao Gai’s dying injunction, sought to yield the leadership to Squire Lu, but the others refused to accept it. Song Jiang then said, “Our stronghold is presently short of money and grain. East of Liangshan Marsh lie two prefectures where stores of both may be found: one is Dongping Prefecture and the other Dongchang Prefecture. We have never before troubled the common people there, yet if we ask to borrow grain, they will plainly refuse. I shall now prepare two lots, and Squire Lu and I will each draw for one place. Whoever first takes his city shall become lord of Liangshan Marsh. What do you say?” Wu Yong said, “That will do. Let us submit to Heaven’s decree.” Lu Junyi said, “You must not speak so. You alone must remain lord of Liangshan Marsh; I shall obey your commands.” But the matter was no longer for Lu Junyi to decide. They immediately summoned Pei Xuan, the “Iron-Faced Clerk,” and had him prepare two lots. When they had burned incense and prayed to Heaven, each drew one. Song Jiang drew Dongping Prefecture, and Lu Junyi Dongchang Prefecture. No one said a word.

p.src: A banquet was held that day. In the midst of the drinking, Song Jiang issued orders and assigned the men and horses. Under Song Jiang were Lin Chong, Hua Rong, Liu Tang, Shi Jin, Xu Ning, Yan Shun, Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, Han Tao, Peng Qi, Kong Ming, Kong Liang, Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Wang the Short Tiger, “Ten Feet of Blue,” Zhang Qing, Sun Erniang, Sun Xin, Gu Dasao, Shi Yong, Yu Baosi, Wang Dingliu, and Duan Jingzhu—twenty-five leaders great and small, with ten thousand horse and foot. The three naval leaders, Ruan Xiao’er, Ruan Xiaowu, and Ruan Xiaoqi, were to command the marines, sail the boats, and provide support.

p.src: Once the assignments had been settled, Song Jiang and his leaders went to attack Dongping Prefecture, while Lu Junyi and his leaders went to attack Dongchang Prefecture. The many leaders descended the mountain with their respective forces. This took place on the first day of the third month. The day was warm, the breeze mild, the grass green, and the sand soft—a perfect time for battle.

p.src: Now Song Jiang led his army toward Dongping Prefecture and halted at a place called Anshan Town, only forty li from the city, where he encamped his forces. Song Jiang said, “The prefect of Dongping is Cheng Wanli, and there is also a military commander who hails from Shangdang Commandery in Hedong. His surname is Dong and his given name Ping. He is skilled with a pair of spears, and all call him the ‘General of the Twin Spears.’ His valor is such that ten thousand men could not withstand him. Although we mean to attack his city, we should first observe the proper courtesies toward him. Let two men take a letter of challenge there and deliver it. If they are willing to surrender, we can avoid resorting to arms. If they refuse to obey, we may then unleash the slaughter, and none will have cause to blame us. Who dares go first and deliver the letter for me?” At this, a man from among his followers stepped forward, ten feet tall and several spans about the waist. Who was this man? A poem bears witness: Wealth he loved not, righteousness alone; like a temple guardian in form and bone. For his great height they call him the God of the Perilous Way; this is Yu Baosi of Qingzhou.

p.src: Meanwhile, Prefect Cheng of Dongping learned that Song Jiang had raised an army and encamped at Anshan Town, so he summoned Dong Ping, the prefecture’s military commander known as the “General of the Twin Spears,” to discuss this grave military affair. While they were seated, a doorkeeper reported, “Song Jiang has sent men to deliver a letter of challenge.” Prefect Cheng ordered them brought in. Yu Baosi and Wang Dingliu appeared before him in the prefectural hall and presented the letter. After reading it, Cheng Wanli said to Military Commander Dong, “They want to borrow money and grain from this prefecture. What are we to do?” Dong Ping flew into a rage upon hearing this and ordered the envoys dragged out and beheaded at once. Prefect Cheng said, “You must not. Since ancient times it has been said, ‘When two states are at war, their envoys are not slain.’ To kill them would violate propriety. Give each man twenty strokes of the interrogation cudgel and send them back to their stronghold. Then we shall see what their people do.” Dong Ping’s fury remained unabated. He shouted for Yu Baosi and Wang Dingliu to be bound together and thrown down, then had them beaten until their skin split and flesh burst before driving them out of the city. The two returned to the main camp and tearfully complained to Song Jiang, “That scoundrel Dong Ping is utterly discourteous! He holds our stronghold in the greatest contempt!”

p.src: When Song Jiang saw how the two had been beaten, rage filled his breast, and he wished to swallow the whole prefecture at a stroke. First he ordered Yu Baosi and Wang Dingliu placed in a cart and sent back to the mountain to recuperate. Then Shi Jin, the “Nine-Dragoned,” rose and said, “When I lived in Dongping Prefecture, I was intimate with a courtesan in the pleasure quarter named Li Ruilan, and we came to know each other well. I shall now take plenty of gold and silver, slip secretly into the city, and lodge at her house. Let us agree upon a day and hour, and then, elder brother, you may attack the city. As soon as Dong Ping comes out to give battle, I shall climb the drum tower and set it ablaze. With our forces working together from within and without, the great enterprise will succeed.” Song Jiang said, “Excellent.” Shi Jin immediately gathered gold and silver into a bundle, concealed weapons about his person, took his leave with a bow, and set out. Song Jiang said, “Brother, watch carefully for your opportunity. I shall keep the army here and make no move for now.”

p.src: Now Shi Jin made his way into the city and went straight to Li Ruilan’s house in the western entertainment quarter. When the old man saw that it was Shi Jin, he started in surprise, then ushered him inside and called his daughter out to meet him. Li Ruilan was a woman of extraordinary elegance, refined beyond the common world. A poem bears witness: Her myriad charms no mortal can withstand; like pear blossom bathed in rain, her jade form breathes fragrance. A kingfisher’s cry awakens the dream of Luofu; one might think her a plum blossom adorned for the dawn.

p.src: Li Ruilan led him upstairs and seated him, then asked Shi Jin, “Why have I not seen hide nor hair of you for so long? I heard that you had become a chieftain at Liangshan Marsh and that the authorities had posted notices for your arrest. For the past two days the streets have been in an uproar with talk that Song Jiang means to attack the city for provisions. How is it that you have come here?” Shi Jin said, “I will hide nothing from you. I am now a chieftain at Liangshan Marsh, but I have yet to distinguish myself. Our elder brother is preparing to attack the city for provisions, and I told him all about your household. I have come expressly to act as a spy. Here is a bundle of gold and silver for you, but on no account must you let word of this escape. Once the affair is over tomorrow, I shall take your whole family up the mountain to live happily with us.” Li Ruilan agreed evasively and accepted the gold and silver. After arranging wine and meat for him, she went to consult her mother: “When he used to visit us, he was a decent man, and there was no harm in his coming and going here. But now he has become an outlaw; if the matter comes to light, it will be no laughing matter.” Her father said, “Song Jiang and those heroes of Liangshan Marsh are not to be trifled with. Whenever they attack a city, they invariably take it. If we betray him, then when they break into the city one day, will they let us off?” The old procuress cursed him: “You senile fool! What do you understand of worldly affairs? As the old saying goes, ‘When a bee crawls inside your robe, strip it off and drive the creature out.’ It is the universal rule that whoever turns himself in is absolved of his original offense. Hurry to Dongping Prefecture and inform against him, so that we are spared being implicated later.” Master Li said, “He has given our family so much gold and silver. If we are not to shoulder some risk for him, what did he pay us for?” The old procuress cursed him: “You old beast! What you say is nothing but wind! Families in our profession have brought ruin upon tens of thousands of men. Why should one more make any difference? If you will not go and report him, I shall go to the yamen myself and lodge a complaint—and I shall name you as an accomplice too.” Master Li said, “Do not fly into a rage. Have our daughter keep him occupied, and do not ‘beat the grass and startle the snake,’ lest he escape. I shall inform the constables and have them come arrest him first; then I will make the formal accusation.”

p.src: Now when Shi Jin saw Li Ruilan come back upstairs, her face flushing and paling by turns, he asked, “Has something happened in your house? Why do you look so alarmed?” Li Ruilan replied, “Just now, as I was climbing the stairs, I missed a step and nearly fell. That is why my heart is still pounding and I am so flustered.” Brave though Shi Jin was, he was deceived by her and suspected nothing further. A poem bears witness: Alas, how many are the tricks of the green bower; in the end, the painted courtesan protects the old procuress. Had he known she secretly plotted treachery, he would not have squandered gold to purchase smiles and song.

p.src: As Li Ruilan spoke with him of their feelings after the long separation, scarcely an hour had passed when footsteps sounded by the stairs and someone came rushing up. A hue and cry arose outside the window, and dozens of constables stormed upstairs. Caught wholly unprepared, Shi Jin was seized like a sparrow in an eagle’s talons or a turtledove struck by a pellet. They bound the mighty man as helplessly as a lion with its head clutched, dragged him downstairs, and marched him straight to the hall of Dongping Prefecture.

p.src: Prefect Cheng looked at him and cursed: “You have audacity enough to fill your whole body! How dare you come here alone as a spy? Had Li Ruilan’s father not informed against you, you would have brought disaster upon all the innocent people of my prefecture! Confess your purpose at once! What did Song Jiang send you here to do?” Shi Jin said not a word. Dong Ping said, “How will a hard-boned bandit like this ever confess unless he is beaten?” Prefect Cheng shouted, “Lay into the rogue with all your strength!” Jailers and prison guards came forward from both sides. First they sprayed cold water over his legs, then dealt each leg a hundred heavy strokes. Shi Jin let them torture him but would not confess the truth. Dong Ping said, “Put the rogue in a long cangue and wooden shackles and send him to death row. When Song Jiang has been captured, send them both to the capital for punishment.”

p.src: Now after Shi Jin had departed, Song Jiang wrote a letter telling Wu Yong all the particulars. When Wu Yong read Song Gongming’s letter—which said that Shi Jin had gone to the house of the courtesan Li Ruilan to act as a spy—he was greatly alarmed. He hurried to tell Lu Junyi, then traveled through the night to see Song Jiang and asked, “Who told Shi Jin to go?” Song Jiang replied, “He volunteered to go himself. He said that Head Courtesan Li was his former mistress and that their attachment ran deep; that was why he went.” Wu Yong said, “Elder brother, you showed too little judgment. Had I been here, I would never have let him go. As the common saying goes, ‘A courtesan’s household—those who know its shame omit five words.’ They make easy use of practiced familiarity, welcoming the new and seeing off the old; how many talented men have they ruined? Moreover, their affections are as fickle as water. However much tenderness there may be, they can hardly escape the old procuress’s control. Now that he has gone there, he is certain to come to grief!” Song Jiang then asked Wu Yong for a plan. Wu Yong called Gu Dasao and said, “I must trouble you to make a journey. Disguise yourself as a poor old woman, slip into the city, and pretend to be a beggar. If there is any news, return with all speed. If Shi Jin has been cast into prison, speak to the jailer and say, ‘We share an old attachment, and I wish to bring him a mouthful of food.’ Press your way into the prison and secretly tell Shi Jin, ‘On the last night of the month, around dusk, we shall certainly come to attack the city. Near the place where water and fire are kept, you must devise a way to escape.’ On the last night of the month, start a fire inside the city as our signal. Only then can our troops advance and the affair succeed. Elder brother, first attack Wenshang County; the common people will surely all flee to Dongping Prefecture. Then have Gu Dasao mingle among them and enter the city in the confusion; no one will notice her.” Having laid his plan, Wu Yong mounted his horse and returned at once to Dongchang Prefecture.

p.src: Now Gu Dasao, her hair disheveled and her clothes in tatters, mingled with the crowd, slipped into the city, and went begging through the streets. When she reached the prefectural offices, she made inquiries and learned that Shi Jin was indeed confined in prison; only then did she realize that Wu Yong's foresight was unfailing. The next day, carrying a food jar, she lingered to and fro outside the prison office, watching for an opportunity. Seeing an elderly warder emerge from the prison, Gu Dasao immediately bowed to him, tears streaming down her face. The elderly warder asked, “Why are you crying, you poor old woman?” Gu Dasao replied, “Shi Dalang, who is imprisoned here, was once my master. It has already been ten years since we parted. I had only heard that he was traveling the rivers and lakes in trade; I do not know what brought him to prison. Plainly there is no one to bring him food, so I begged this little portion and came especially to ease his hunger. Good sir, take pity and lead me inside. The merit would surpass that of building a seven-story pagoda!” The warder said, “He is a bandit from Liangshan Marsh, guilty of a capital crime. Who would dare take you inside?” Gu Dasao said, “Even if he must suffer the knife and the slicing blade, let him at least accept his fate with his eyes closed in peace. Only take pity and lead this old woman in, so I may give him this mouthful of food and show that our former bond is not forgotten.” When she had finished, she wept again. The elderly warder thought, “Were this a man, it would be difficult to take him inside, but what harm can one woman do? …” He then led Gu Dasao straight into the prison, where she saw Shi Jin with a heavy cangue around his neck and iron chains about his waist. At the sight of Gu Dasao, Shi Jin was greatly startled, but dared not utter a sound. Gu Dasao pretended to sob while feeding him. Another jail officer came over and shouted, “This is a condemned villain! ‘No breath of air passes through a prison’—who let you come and bring him food? Get out at once, or you will receive two strokes of the cudgel!” Seeing so many people in the prison, Gu Dasao could not explain the details and managed only to say, “On the last night of the month we will storm the city. You must fight your own way out of the prison.” When Shi Jin tried to ask more, a junior jailer beat Gu Dasao out through the prison gate. Shi Jin remembered only the words “the last night of the month.”

u.src: Now Gu Dasao, her hair disheveled and her clothes in tatters, mingled with the crowd, slipped into the city, and went begging through the streets.
When she reached the prefectural offices, she made inquiries and learned that Shi Jin was indeed confined in prison; only then did she realize that Wu Yong's foresight was unfailing.
The next day, carrying a food jar, she lingered to and fro outside the prison office, watching for an opportunity.
Seeing an elderly warder emerge from the prison, Gu Dasao immediately bowed to him, tears streaming down her face.
The elderly warder asked, “Why are you crying, you poor old woman?”
Gu Dasao replied, “Shi Dalang, who is imprisoned here, was once my master.
It has already been ten years since we parted.
I had only heard that he was traveling the rivers and lakes in trade; I do not know what brought him to prison.
Plainly there is no one to bring him food, so I begged this little portion and came especially to ease his hunger.
Good sir, take pity and lead me inside. The merit would surpass that of building a seven-story pagoda!”
The warder said, “He is a bandit from Liangshan Marsh, guilty of a capital crime. Who would dare take you inside?”
Gu Dasao said, “Even if he must suffer the knife and the slicing blade, let him at least accept his fate with his eyes closed in peace.
Only take pity and lead this old woman in, so I may give him this mouthful of food and show that our former bond is not forgotten.”
When she had finished, she wept again.
The elderly warder thought, “Were this a man, it would be difficult to take him inside, but what harm can one woman do?
…” He then led Gu Dasao straight into the prison, where she saw Shi Jin with a heavy cangue around his neck and iron chains about his waist.

Gu Dasao pretended to sob while feeding him.
Another jail officer came over and shouted, “This is a condemned villain!

Get out at once, or you will receive two strokes of the cudgel!”

p.src: Now that third month happened to have thirty days. On the twenty-ninth, Shi Jin heard two jailers talking in the prison and asked, “What day is it today?” The junior jailer had remembered wrongly and answered, “Today is the last day of the month. Later tonight I must buy a packet of spirit money to burn.” Hearing this, Shi Jin could hardly wait for nightfall. A junior jailer, half drunk, took Shi Jin to the latrine pit. Shi Jin tricked him by saying, “Who is that behind you?” As soon as the man turned his head, Shi Jin wrenched himself free and struck him squarely in the face with one end of the cangue, knocking him to the ground. He picked up a brick, smashed open his wooden fetters, glared like a hawk, and charged into the central guard pavilion. The warders were all drunk; Shi Jin struck them head-on, killing some while the rest fled. He forced open the prison gate and waited only for help from outside. He also released every prisoner in the jail, some fifty or sixty in all. They raised a great cry within the prison and escaped together.

p.src: When someone reported this to the prefect, Cheng Wanli turned ashen with fright and hurriedly summoned the military commissioner to confer. Dong Ping said, “There must be spies inside the city. First send a large force to surround these bandits. Meanwhile, I shall seize this opportunity to lead the army out of the city and capture Song Jiang. Your Excellency must guard the city closely. Send several dozen warders to encircle the prison gate and let none escape.” Dong Ping mounted his horse, mustered the troops, and departed. Prefect Cheng then assembled all the jail officers, attendants, and guards. Armed with spears and cudgels, they went before the main prison and raised a clamor. Inside the prison, Shi Jin dared not venture out rashly. Those outside, for their part, dared not enter. Gu Dasao could only lament bitterly.

p.src: Meanwhile, Military Commissioner Dong Ping mustered his troops, mounted at the fourth watch, and charged toward Song Jiang's camp. A scout posted along the road reported the news to Song Jiang. Song Jiang said, “Gu Dasao must have met with fresh trouble inside the city. Since they are attacking, prepare to meet the enemy.” At the command, all the troops rose. Day was just breaking when they met Dong Ping's forces. The two sides drew up their battle lines, and Dong Ping rode forth—a peerless hero, surpassing others in both strategy and courage. A poem bears witness: Two bannered emblems gleamed beneath the sun; his silver-chased iron armor seemed coated with frost. His polished phoenix-winged helmet shone white; his brocade qilin battle coat was green. A pair of white dragons vied high and low; two silver pythons flew in turn. The gallant and dashing warrior from east of the Yellow River—he who wields the twin spears is Dong Ping.

p.src: Dong Ping was clever and quick-witted, versed in every school of thought and every walk of life. He could play wind instruments and tune strings with equal skill, and throughout Shandong and Hebei he was known as the “Dashing General of the Twin Spears.” From before the battle line, Song Jiang observed Dong Ping's striking appearance and bearing and took a liking to him at first sight; then he noticed a small banner thrust into Dong Ping's quiver, bearing the couplet: “Heroic general of the twin spears; dashing lord of ten thousand households.” Song Jiang sent Han Tao forth to meet him. Wielding his iron lance, Han Tao charged straight at Dong Ping, but Dong Ping's pair of iron spears moved with uncanny and unpredictable skill, and no man could withstand him. Song Jiang then ordered Xu Ning, the “Golden Lancer,” to take his hooked sickle spear and relieve Han Tao. Xu Ning galloped out and engaged Dong Ping in combat. The two fought fifty bouts on the battlefield without either gaining the upper hand. After they had fought for a long time, Song Jiang feared some mishap might befall Xu Ning and ordered the gong sounded for withdrawal. Xu Ning reined in and turned back, but Dong Ping raised his twin spears and pursued him straight into the formation. Song Jiang flicked the tip of his whip, and the troops closed around Dong Ping from every side. Song Jiang reined his horse atop a rise and watched as Dong Ping was hemmed in within the formation. Whenever Dong Ping made eastward, Song Jiang pointed his signal flag east, and the troops moved east to surround him; whenever he made westward, the signal flag pointed west, and the troops moved west to encircle him. Dong Ping charged this way and that within the formation, killing with his two spears until after the hour of the monkey. At last he broke open a path and fought his way out. Song Jiang did not pursue him. Unable to win the battle, Dong Ping withdrew his troops that evening and returned to the city. Song Jiang mobilized his forces during the night, advanced directly to the city walls, and deployed his troops in a complete encirclement. Inside the city, Gu Dasao did not yet dare set any fires, while Shi Jin was still unable to get out. Thus the two sides remained locked in opposition.

p.src: Now Prefect Cheng had a daughter of exceptional beauty; Dong Ping had no wife and repeatedly sent matchmakers to seek her hand, but Cheng Wanli would not consent; because of this, though their daily words were cordial, their hearts were not in harmony. That evening, after leading his troops back into the city, Dong Ping sent an intimate intermediary to take advantage of the occasion and ask again about the marriage. Prefect Cheng replied, “I am a civil official and he a military officer; to take him into my family as a son-in-law would be entirely fitting. But now bandits are at the city walls and the situation is perilous. If I consented at once, people would mock me. Once the bandit army has been driven off and the city secured from danger, it will not be too late to discuss the marriage.” The intermediary carried this reply back to Dong Ping. Though Dong Ping answered aloud, “That is reasonable,” he remained troubled at heart and was far from pleased, fearing that Cheng might still refuse him afterward.

p.src: Here Song Jiang pressed the attack throughout the night, and the prefect repeatedly urged his men to give battle. Dong Ping flew into a rage, donned his armor, mounted his horse, and led the entire army out of the city to engage the enemy. From beneath the commander's banner at the front of the formation, Song Jiang himself shouted, “You are but a solitary general—how can you withstand me? Have you not heard the saying of the ancients: ‘When a great mansion is about to fall, no single timber can support it’? Look upon the hundred thousand valiant troops and thousand fierce commanders beneath me. We act on Heaven's behalf, aiding the distressed and supporting those in peril. Come and surrender at once, and I shall spare your life!” Dong Ping furiously retorted, “You tattoo-faced petty clerk, you death-deserving madman! How dare you spout such nonsense!” With that, he raised his twin spears and charged straight at Song Jiang. Lin Chong was on the left and Hua Rong on the right. Both commanders rode out together, each wielding his weapon, and met Dong Ping in combat. After exchanging several bouts, the two commanders turned and fled. Song Jiang's forces feigned defeat and scattered in flight. Eager to win distinction, Dong Ping spurred his horse in pursuit. Song Jiang and his men happened to retreat as far as the boundary of Shouchun County, Song Jiang fleeing ahead and Dong Ping pursuing behind. More than ten li from the city, they came to a village with thatched cottages on both sides and a post road running down the middle. Unaware that it was a ruse, Dong Ping thought only of galloping after them. Seeing how formidable Dong Ping was, Song Jiang had sent Wang the Stumpy Tiger, “Ten Feet of Blue” Hu Sanniang, Zhang Qing, and Sun Erniang ahead the previous night with more than a hundred men to lie in ambush among the cottages on both sides. They had stretched several horse-tripping ropes across the road and concealed them beneath a thin layer of earth. When he arrived, a gong was to sound, all the ropes were to be raised at once, and Dong Ping was to be captured. As Dong Ping pursued them and reached that place, he suddenly heard Kong Ming and Kong Liang shouting behind him, “Do not harm our lord!” Just as he reached the cottages, a gong sounded, the doors on both sides flew open, and the ropes were hauled taut. His horse was just about to turn when the tripping ropes behind it all rose at once, bringing the animal down and throwing Dong Ping from the saddle. From the left burst “Ten Feet of Blue” and Wang the Stumpy Tiger; from the right came Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang. All four rushed upon Dong Ping and seized him. They took his helmet, armor, twin spears, and horse, leaving him nothing. The two female chieftains seized Dong Ping, twisted his arms behind his back, and bound him with hemp rope. Each holding a steel saber, the two women escorted Dong Ping under guard to Song Jiang.

p.src: Meanwhile, after passing the cottages, Song Jiang reined in his horse and stood beneath a green poplar, where he met the two female chieftains escorting Dong Ping toward him. Song Jiang immediately ordered the two women back, crying, “I told you to invite General Dong here. Who told you to bring him bound?” The two women murmured their obedience and withdrew. Song Jiang hurriedly dismounted and personally untied him. He then removed his own protective armor and brocade robe, put them on Dong Ping, and bowed low before him. Dong Ping hastily returned the courtesy. Song Jiang said, “If you, General, do not disdain one so lowly as I, I ask you to become a master of our mountain stronghold.” Dong Ping replied, “I am a captured man; even ten thousand deaths would be too light a punishment! If I am pardoned and granted a place of refuge, it will truly be the greatest good fortune.” Song Jiang said, “Our humble stronghold adjoins the marsh, and we have never made a practice of troubling the people. We have come specially to Dongping Prefecture to borrow provisions only because our grain stores are short. We have no other purpose.” Dong Ping said, “That scoundrel Cheng Wanli was originally a household tutor in Tong Guan's establishment. Having secured this fine appointment, how could he fail to oppress the common people? If you will permit me, elder brother, I shall go now and trick them into opening the city gate. Then we can storm the city and seize its money and grain together, and thus I may repay your kindness.”

p.src: Song Jiang was overjoyed. He immediately ordered his men to bring Dong Ping's helmet, armor, spears, and horse and return them to him, whereupon Dong Ping armed himself and mounted. Dong Ping led the way, with Song Jiang's troops behind. Their banners furled, they all arrived beneath the walls of Dongping. At the head of the troops Dong Ping shouted, “Open the city gate at once!” When the gate guards shone their torches upon him, they recognized Military Controller Dong and immediately threw the gate wide and lowered the drawbridge. Dong Ping spurred his horse through first and hacked apart the iron chain; behind him, Song Jiang and the others drove their men and horses straight into the city. Once they had reached the Dongping prefectural offices, an urgent order was issued forbidding anyone to kill the common people, set fires, or burn their homes. Dong Ping made straight for the prefect's private residence, killed every member of Prefect Cheng's household, and took his daughter. Song Jiang first ordered the prison opened and rescued Shi Jin. Then he opened the government treasuries and took all the gold, silver, valuables, and silks. He threw open the granaries, loaded the rice and grain onto carts, and sent men ahead to escort it to Golden Sands Beach at Liangshan Marsh, where it was delivered to the three Ruan chieftains and relayed up the mountain. Shi Jin personally led men to Li Ruilan's house in the Western Entertainment Quarter and hacked the old procuress, young and old alike, and her entire household to pieces. Song Jiang distributed the prefect's family property among the residents and posted proclamations along the streets, informing the people: “The prefectural official who harmed the people has already been put to death. You good people must each return peacefully to your livelihoods.” When the proclamations had been issued, they marshaled their forces and withdrew.
